title: Primary Clarification of CHO Harvested Cell Culture Fluid using an Acoustic Separator
protocol: Connect the turbidity cables into their respective ports labeled as F, 1, 2, 3, 4.
Connect the chamber power BNC cables to the back of the AWS system labeled as 1, 2, 3, 4.
Insert the turbidity probes into the turbidity meter and thermometer housing.
Tighten the screws on the turbidity probes.
Connect the feed tubing to the input of the feed turbidity port via the feed pump.
Connect the y-tubing from the output of the feed turbidity port to the inlet ports of the acoustophoretic chamber.
Connect the stage1 tubing from the waste port of the acoustophoretic chamber via the stage1 pump to a cell collection vessel.
Connect the tubing from the permeate port of the acoustophoretic chamber to the input of probe1 turbidity port.
Connect the harvest tubing from the probe1 turbidity port to a product collection vessel.
Prime the system with HCCF.
Turn on the power switches of the AWS.
Double-click the desk icon for the associated software.
Press the “Start Test” button in the “Readings” panel to initiate data recording.
Connect the feed tubing end into the HCCF vessel being stirred.
Enter the pump rate on the “Controls” screen within the “Feed Pump Image.”
Ensure that the “Pump Direction Arrow Icon” is correctly selected for pumping HCCF from the vessel into the acoustophoretic chamber.
Click on the “Triangle Icon” next to “Turn ON” under the Feed Pump Image to start the pump.
Monitor the feed turbidity measurements by observing the “Percent Reduction Panel” during the filling of the acoustophoretic chamber.
Press “Turn OFF” within the gray box under the Feed Pump Image to stop the pump once the liquid is above the piezo transducer at the back of the acoustophoretic chamber.
Connect the BNC power cable to the acoustophoretic chamber.
Change the rate of feed pump to the desired operating rate after filling and connecting the power cable.
Turn on the stage1 piezo power by sliding the bar in the power module to 10 W.
Press the “Turn ON” icon on the right side of the Stage 1 box.
Start the stage1 pump with an appropriate rate based on the cell density and feed pump rate.
Tare a scale with an empty 15 mL tube.
Fill the tube with feed material and record the total weight of the tube with feed.
Centrifuge the tube for 10 min at 3,700 x g.
Decant the supernatant into a separate container.
Measure the weight of the tube with the cell pellet.
Calculate the packed cell mass percentage of the feed material using the formula (decanted tube weight/filled tube weight) x 100%.
Monitor the turbidity profile of stage1 turbidity as the overflow from the acoustophoretic chamber enters the turbidity probe.
Monitor the temperature difference between feed and stage1 during cell separation.
Increase feed flow rate if the temperature rises due to higher cell density feed.
Stop the feed pump by pressing Turn OFF within the gray box under the feed pump image.
Stop the stage1 pump by pressing Turn OFF within the gray box under the stage1 pump image.
Turn off the power to the chamber by pressing Turn OFF on the right side of the Stage 1 box.
Disconnect the BNC power cable from the chamber.
Collect product harvest material for further clarification and purification procedures.
Discard cell harvest material.
Drain the remaining fluid in the acoustophoretic chamber by placing the waste tubing into an empty vessel.
Disconnect the tubing from the acoustophoretic chamber inlet and permeate ports.
Release the waste tubing from the pump head.
Reconnect the tubing and place the waste tubing back into the pump head.
Flow through DI water from the end of feed tubing using a feed pump rate of 60 mL/min and stage1 pump rate of 60 mL/min for 15–20 min.
Discard the flow through.
Pump 70% isopropyl alcohol (IPA) through the tubing and the chamber using the feed pump for 15–20 min.
Discard the flow through.
Repeat cleaning procedure with DI water to clear the tubes and the chamber by using the feed pump for 15–20 min.
Discard the flow through.
Disassemble the tubing from the turbidity probes and acoustophoretic chambers.
Clean the area with 70% IPA.
Disassemble the turbidity probes.
Clean inside the turbidity probes with 70% IPA.
Let all parts air dry.
Reassemble for the next use.
